text:
Anna: Heads-up — found a weird case during a rolling upgrade where tenant residency flipped twice for the same prefix, causing duplicate KV reads. Reproduced on staging.
Sam: Can you paste the minimal repro? sounds like lease churn + race in the handoff path.
Anna: repro log snippet:
```
[2026-03-18T09:12:11Z] lease_acquire tenant=acme prefix=usr:123 owner=node-a lease_id=42
[2026-03-18T09:12:12Z] lease_release tenant=acme prefix=usr:123 owner=node-a
[2026-03-18T09:12:12Z] lease_acquire tenant=acme prefix=usr:123 owner=node-b lease_id=1
[2026-03-18T09:12:12Z] lease_acquire tenant=acme prefix=usr:123 owner=node-a lease_id=43
```
Anna: node-a reacquired before node-b fully applied residency table. reads ended up hitting both caches and we saw duplicate incremental apply logs.
Priya: That matches the prefetch/eviction race we chatted about, but this is during upgrade (containers restarting with new binary). Are we dealing with non-idempotent apply operations?
Maya: We do have a non-idempotent side effect in the LRU residency counters — increment-only. If two nodes think they own it briefly, counters double-count and eviction heuristics get confused.
Jorge: Two potential fixes: (1) add stable ownership tokens that outlive transient restarts (so an acquire has monotonic token), or (2) make apply idempotent by including origin token and ignore replays.
Sam: I prefer (2) — idempotency buys us correctness across other failure modes too. But it's more invasive: plumbing tokens through apply/replicate paths and persisting token in the slab metadata.
Priya: (1) seems lower-change: persist a tiny owner-token in the lease manager backend (etcd) so when the node restarts it can attempt to recover same token. But still doesn't avoid the race where node-b gets the lease first.
Anna: Right — token persistence avoids duplicate owner churn during restarts but doesn't solve concurrent reacquire by two nodes if network partitions occur.
Maya: We sketched a hybrid: assign a stable prefix-owner id (UUID) at first-write, persist in the prefix metadata, and treat it as the canonical authority for short windows. Ownership handoff requires explicit transfer operation that'll fail fast if token mismatch.
Jorge: That allows idempotent apply if we include owner-id in the apply log. On replay, if owner-id doesn't match current prefix-owner, we drop/redirect. Fewer changes to the hot path.
Sam: Performance cost: extra owner-id check on every apply and one extra small write on first assignment and handoff. OK if owner-id is 16 bytes.
Priya: Also think about backward compatibility with older nodes during canary. The plan should gracefully degrade: if owner-id absent, fallback to the old lease semantics.
Anna: Agree. We need a canary rollout plan: stage 1 write owner-id but still accept legacy replays; stage 2 enforce owner-id checks; stage 3 remove legacy path.
Maya: Ops runbook: if we see "double-apply" alerts, diag by searching for apply entries with differing owner-ids for same seq. Short-term mitigation is to throttle handoff frequency and extend lease handshake timeout.
Jorge: Add metric: prefix_owner_conflict_count and prefix_apply_ignored{reason="owner_mismatch"}. Also expose a debug endpoint to snapshot prefix metadata for audits.
Sam: One subtlety: what about prefix splitting/compaction? Owner-id probably needs to survive split; parent keeps same owner unless explicitly transferred.
Priya: Good point — add transfer semantics to compaction flow.
Anna: Next steps: Anna + Maya to draft a tiny RFC with the hybrid owner-id + idempotent-apply approach. Sam to estimate perf/regressions. Jorge to propose metrics and runbook additions.
ops-bot: Deploy window reserved: 2026-03-24 02:00-04:00 UTC for canary rollouts. :white_check_mark:
Anna: Thanks — will post the RFC link in this thread when ready. :thumbsup:
